```{r}
#| label: build functions
#| echo: false
#| eval: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| results: hide

parse_scfa <- function(subset_pattern = NULL, path = "./") {
  file_list <- list.files(pattern = "*.xls", path)
  sequence_list <- list()
  for (i in 1:(length(file_list))) {
    sequence_list[[file_list[i]]] <- data.frame(read_xls(path = paste(path, file_list[[i]], sep = ""), skip = 39, sheet = "Integration"))
  }
  samples <- list()
  for (j in 1:length(file_list)) {
    samples[[file_list[j]]] <- sequence_list[[file_list[j]]][-c(1, 2), c("Peak.Name", "Amount")]
    samples[[file_list[j]]]$Amount <- as.numeric(as.character(samples[[file_list[j]]]$Amount))
    colnames(samples[[file_list[j]]])[2] <- file_list[j]
  }
  for (l in 1:length(file_list)) {
    samples[[file_list[l]]] <- samples[[file_list[l]]][which(!is.na(samples[[file_list[l]]]$Peak.Name)), ]
  }
  if (is.null(subset_pattern)) {
    subset_samples <- samples
  } else {
    subset_samples <- samples[which(grepl(pattern = subset_pattern, x = names(samples)))]
  }
  table <- subset_samples[[1]]
  for (k in 2:length(subset_samples)) {
    table <- join(table, subset_samples[[k]], "Peak.Name")
  }

  # REMOVES UNKNOWN PEAKS AND INTERNAL STANDARD
  table <- table[which(!table$Peak.Name %in% ""), ]
  colnames(table) <- gsub(pattern = ".xls", replacement = "", x = colnames(table))
  table <- table[which(!table$Peak.Name %in% c("Component 2", "2-Ethylbutyric Acid")), ]

  rownames(table) <- table$Peak.Name
  table$Peak.Name <- NULL
  parsed_table <- data.frame(t(table))
  parsed_table$Sample <- row.names(parsed_table)
  parsed_table[is.na(parsed_table)] <- 0
  return(parsed_table)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: prepare the plots and perform statistics
#| results: asis
#| message: false
#| echo: false
#| eval: true


coldats <- c("MBI.Sample.ID", "Subject_ID", "Group", "Time", Variables)

exportdat <- normalized_poop %>% select(all_of(coldats))
# colnames(exportdat)[which(colnames(exportdat) %in% Variables)]

########################################################################################

melt_poop <- reshape2::melt(
  data = normalized_poop,
  measure.vars = Variables
)


scfa_subset <- list()
scfa_bp <- list()
poop_aov <- list()
poop_lmer <- list()
scfa_lmer <- list()
scfa_Coeff <- list()

scfa_anova <- list()
scfa_tukey <- list()
scfa_aov <- list()
tukey1 <- list()
tukey2 <- list()
tukey3 <- list()
foo <- list()
group_contrasts <- list()
time_contrasts <- list()


########################################################################################
################################### ---Box-Plot----######################################

for (var in Variables) {
  scfa_subset[[var]] <- melt_poop %>% filter(variable %in% var)
  temp <- scfa_subset[[var]]

  scfa_bp[[var]] <- ggplot(data = temp) +
    geom_boxplot(aes(x = !!sym(x_factor), y = value), outlier.alpha = 0) +
    ggtitle(label = var) +
    ylab(scfa_ylab) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 1)) +
    geom_jitter(aes(x = !!sym(x_factor), y = value, color = !!sym(x_factor)),
      width  = 0.2,
      height = 0,
      alpha  = 0.7,
      size   = 2
    ) +
    scale_color_manual(values = colours5)

  if (!is.null(facet_factor)) {
    scfa_bp[[var]] <- scfa_bp[[var]] +
      facet_grid(eval(parse(text = paste("~", facet_factor))),
        scales = "free",
        drop = T,
        space = "free_x"
      )
  }

  if (!is.null(lmer.formula)) {
    temp <- temp %>% tidyr::drop_na(value, Group, Time, Subject_ID)
    temp$Subject_ID <- factor(temp$Subject_ID)
    temp$Group <- factor(temp$Group, levels = levels(melt_poop$Group))
    temp$Time <- factor(temp$Time, levels = levels(melt_poop$Time))
    # Run the linear mixed model (ADDITIVE)
    fit <- tryCatch(
      lmer(formula = eval(parse(text = lmer.formula)), data = temp),
      error = identity
    )
    if (inherits(fit, "error")) {
      poop_lmer[[var]] <- NULL
      scfa_lmer[[var]] <- NULL
      scfa_Coeff[[var]] <- data.frame(
        Term = "Model",
        Message = fit$message
      )
      scfa_anova[[var]] <- NULL
      group_contrasts[[var]] <- NULL
      time_contrasts[[var]] <- NULL
    } else {
      poop_lmer[[var]] <- fit
      scfa_lmer[[var]] <- summary(fit)
      coef_tbl <- scfa_lmer[[var]]$coefficients %>%
        as.data.frame() %>%
        tibble::rownames_to_column("Term")
      scfa_Coeff[[var]] <- coef_tbl
      scfa_anova[[var]] <- anova(fit, type = 3) %>%
        as.data.frame() %>%
        tibble::rownames_to_column("Term")
      emm_group <- emmeans::emmeans(fit, ~ Group | Time)
      group_contrasts[[var]] <- as.data.frame(pairs(emm_group, adjust = "tukey"))
      emm_time <- emmeans::emmeans(fit, ~ Time | Group)
      time_contrasts[[var]] <- as.data.frame(pairs(emm_time, adjust = "tukey"))
    }
  }


  if (!is.null(aov.formula)) {
    # Run the ANOVA on your model (ADDITIVE)
    poop_aov[[var]] <- aov(formula = eval(parse(text = aov.formula)), data = temp)
    scfa_aov[[var]] <- anova(poop_aov[[var]])


    tukey1[[var]] <- TukeyHSD(poop_aov[[var]], which = aov.predictor1)
    tukey1[[var]] <- data.frame(tukey1[[var]][[aov.predictor1]])
    tukey1[[var]] <- tukey1[[var]][order(row.names(tukey1[[var]]), decreasing = T), ]
  }
}
```

```{r}
#| label: prepare the summary of the SCFA data
#| results: asis
#| message: false
#| echo: false
#| eval: true

tab <- melt_poop %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    SCFA = factor(variable, levels = Variables),
    Group = factor(Group, levels = levels(metad$Group)),
    Time = factor(Time, levels = levels(metad$Time))
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(SCFA, Group, Time) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    Samples  = sum(!is.na(value)),
    Subjects = dplyr::n_distinct(Subject_ID),
    Mean     = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD       = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    SEM      = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(Samples),
    Min      = min(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    Max      = max(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups  = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(SCFA, Time, Group)
```

# Summary of SCFA data (`r scfa_ylab`)

This study evaluates plasma SCFAs in an elderly cohort, contrasting Control and COVID groups across baseline (T0), 6-month (T1), and 12-month (T2) collections. Subject identifiers were derived from the submitted sample IDs to track individuals longitudinally. Short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) data were analyzed using gas chromatography coupled with a flame ionization detector (GC-FID). The concentrations of individual fatty acids are presented in the following figures. All concentrations were normalized to the amount of input material (`r scfa_ylab`).

 </br>

## Statistical analysis
::: panel-tabset

```{r}
#| label: data analysis
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
#| warning: false
#| message: false


for (var in names(scfa_bp)) {
  cat("\n###", var, "\n")
  if (stats == "1") {
    cat("ANOVA analysis\n")
    knitr::kable(scfa_aov[[var]], align = "c", digits = 3) %>%
      kableExtra::kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive")) %>%
      print()
  }
  if (stats == "2") {
    cat("Linear mixed model: value ~ Group * Time + (1 | Subject_ID)\n")
    if (!is.null(poop_lmer[[var]])) {
      if (!is.null(scfa_anova[[var]]) && nrow(scfa_anova[[var]]) > 0) {
        cat("\n#### Fixed effects (Type III ANOVA)\n")
        knitr::kable(
          scfa_anova[[var]],
          digits = 3
        ) %>%
          kableExtra::kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive")) %>%
          print()
      }
      if (!is.null(scfa_Coeff[[var]]) && nrow(scfa_Coeff[[var]]) > 0 && "Estimate" %in% colnames(scfa_Coeff[[var]])) {
        cat("\n#### Model coefficients\n")
        coef_view <- scfa_Coeff[[var]] %>%
          select(Term, Estimate, `Std. Error`, df, `t value`, `Pr(>|t|)`) %>%
          dplyr::rename(`p value` = `Pr(>|t|)`)
        knitr::kable(
          coef_view,
          digits = 3
        ) %>%
          kableExtra::kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive")) %>%
          print()
      }
    } else if (!is.null(scfa_Coeff[[var]]) && "Message" %in% colnames(scfa_Coeff[[var]])) {
      cat("\n> Model fitting issue: ", scfa_Coeff[[var]]$Message[1], "\n", sep = "")
    }
  }

  if (stats == "1") {
    cat("\n####", "Treatment effect on", aov.predictor1, "\n")
    knitr::kable(tukey1[[var]][, c("diff", "p.adj")], digits = 3) %>%
      kableExtra::kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive")) %>%
      print()
  }


  ## Post-hoc pairwise comparisons
  if (stats == "2") {
    if (!is.null(group_contrasts[[var]]) && nrow(group_contrasts[[var]]) > 0) {
      cat("\n#### Group contrasts within each time point\n")
      knitr::kable(
        group_contrasts[[var]],
        digits = 3
      ) %>%
        kableExtra::kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive")) %>%
        print()
    }
    if (!is.null(time_contrasts[[var]]) && nrow(time_contrasts[[var]]) > 0) {
      cat("\n#### Time contrasts within each group\n")
      knitr::kable(
        time_contrasts[[var]],
        digits = 3
      ) %>%
        kableExtra::kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive")) %>%
        print()
    }
  }
}
```

```{r ,echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, dpi=200}
method <- list()

method[["mouse_feces"]] <- "The procedure for SCFA extraction follows the protocol described by Zhao et al. [-@zhao2006rapid]. Mouse fecal pellets were resuspended in MilliQ-grade water and homogenized using an MP Bio FastPrep system for 1 minute at 4.0 m/s. The suspensions were acidified to a final pH of 2.0 using 5M HCl. After acidification, the suspensions were incubated and centrifuged at 10,000 RPM to separate the supernatant. The resulting supernatant was spiked with 2-ethylbutyric acid to achieve a final concentration of 1 mM."

method[["human_feces"]] <- "The procedure for SCFA extraction follows the protocol described by Zhao et al. [-@zhao2006rapid]. Human fecal samples were resuspended in MilliQ-grade water and homogenized using an MP Bio FastPrep system for 1 minute at 4.0 m/s. The suspensions were acidified to a final pH of 2.0 using 5M HCl. After acidification, the suspensions were incubated and centrifuged at 10,000 RPM to separate the supernatant. The resulting supernatant was spiked with 2-ethylbutyric acid to achieve a final concentration of 1 mM."

method[["feces"]] <- "The procedure for SCFA extraction follows the protocol described by Zhao et al. [-@zhao2006rapid]. Fecal samples were resuspended in MilliQ-grade water and homogenized using an MP Bio FastPrep system for 1 minute at 4.0 m/s. The suspensions were acidified to a final pH of 2.0 using 5M HCl. After acidification, the suspensions were incubated and centrifuged at 10,000 RPM to separate the supernatant. The resulting supernatant was spiked with 2-ethylbutyric acid to achieve a final concentration of 1 mM."

method[["other"]] <- "The procedure for SCFA extraction is based on the protocol described by Zhao et al. [-@zhao2006rapid]. The material was resuspended in MilliQ-grade water and homogenized using an MP Bio FastPrep system for 1 minute at 4.0 m/s. The suspensions were acidified to a final pH of 2.0 using 5M HCl. After acidification, the suspensions were incubated and centrifuged at 10,000 RPM to separate the supernatant. The resulting supernatant was spiked with 2-ethylbutyric acid to achieve a final concentration of 1 mM."
```

`r method[[sample_type]]`
`r if(!sample_type %in% c("mouse feces", "human_feces", "feces")){method[["other"]]}`


Extracted SCFA supernatants were stored in 2-mL gas chromatography (GC) vials equipped with glass inserts. SCFA analysis was performed using a Thermo Trace 1310 gas chromatograph coupled with a flame ionization detector (FID) from Thermo Scientific. Separation was achieved using a Thermo TG-WAXMS A GC column (30 m, 0.32 mm ID, 0.25 µm film thickness), closely following the instrumentation and methodology described in Zhao et al. [-@zhao2006rapid].

The following settings were used for detection:

#### Flame Ionization Detector

* **Temperature:** 240 oC
* **Hydrogen:**	35.0 ml/min
* **Air:**	350.0 ml/min
* **Makeup gas (Nitrogen):**	40.0 ml/min

#### Inlet

* **Carrier pressure:**	225 kPa
* **Column flow:**	6.00 ml/min
* **Purge flow:**	5.00 ml/min
* **Split flow:**	12.0 ml/min
* **Temperature:**	200 oC
* **Splitless time:**	0.75 min

#### Oven
* **Temperature	Gradient:** 100 - 180 oC
* **Gradient time:**	10.0 min
